clauses.quote: The value bound to a scalar-field parameter MUST be a literal admissible for that field
clauses.note: A template call whose expanded-equivalent form puts an inadmissible literal in a scalar field (e.g. manifold) is rejected by that field's own check, reported at the call site.

clauses.quote: The bound value MUST be one a `ranges` tuple entry admits
clauses.note: A template parameter in a faq dense ranges tuple entry is a substitution site; the value it is bound to must be an integer literal or a metaparameter expression, which substitution itself does not check.

clauses.quote: The bound value MUST be a string naming an index set
clauses.note: A template parameter written as the `from` of a faq ranges entry is a substitution site; the value bound to it must name an index set, and an expanded `from` naming no declared set is undefined_index_set at the call site.

clauses.quote: so an author MUST NOT name a parameter after a field literal its body means literally
clauses.note: Authoring policy: the engine must still substitute (next clause), so no verdict depends on it.
clauses.concern: Phrased as an author MUST NOT, yet the same sentence requires bindings to accept and substitute such a body; a violating document is not rejected by anything, so this behaves as a SHOULD and a document can be non-conforming while every conforming tool accepts it.

clauses.quote: bindings MAY surface a lint-grade diagnostic for such a collision but MUST still substitute
clauses.note: Every string in a template body equal to a declared parameter name is replaced on instantiation, including in scalar fields and where it coincides with a field literal or index symbol.

clauses.quote: a rename applied at an `expression_template_imports` edge MUST rewrite the imported templates' `where.*.shape` entries together with the imported `index_sets` and range references
clauses.note: Import-edge index-set renaming maps where.shape entries through the same rename map as the imported index_sets, so a renamed instance's constraints name the renamed sets.
clauses.concern: The §9.7.7 'Transitivity (normative occurrence sites)' list for index-set renames enumerates registry keys, `of`, `from`, wrt/dim/var, integral bounds and join `on`, but not `where.*.shape`; the two normative enumerations of rename sites disagree.

clauses.quote: `args`: MUST be an empty array.
clauses.note: An apply_expression_template node with non-empty args is rejected at load.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is assigned to a non-empty `args`; the §9.6.6 table has no matching row (invalid_declaration covers template declarations, not call sites).

clauses.quote: `match` patterns MUST NOT contain `apply_expression_template` nodes. Because selection
clauses.note: A match pattern containing an apply_expression_template node is rejected at registration.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is named for this rejection here or in §9.7.3, and the §9.6.6 table has no row for it (only possibly the catch-all 'other structural defects' of invalid_declaration).

clauses.quote: all five bindings MUST produce byte-identical fixpoints (or the same non-convergence rejection)
clauses.note: The rewrite fixpoint (outermost-first passes, priority then effective-declaration-order selection, where-filtering before selection, 64-pass bound) is a deterministic function of the loaded document.

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST cover every entry of the template's `params` exactly — no missing keys, no extras.
clauses.note: A call whose bindings key set differs from the template's params set is rejected with apply_expression_template_bindings_mismatch.

clauses.quote: a value substituted into a scalar-field position MUST be a literal admissible for that field, enforced by the §9.6.9 validation discharge
clauses.note: Substitution never checks field admissibility; validation of the expanded-equivalent form rejects an inadmissible scalar-field value.

clauses.quote: Expansion MUST NOT depend on argument evaluation.
clauses.note: Template instantiation is a function of the argument ASTs only: equal ASTs give equal results regardless of their values.

clauses.quote: a loader MUST NOT special-case older versions to recover Option A matching
clauses.note: Rule-4 pattern opacity applies to every accepted document regardless of its declared esm version.

clauses.quote: but MUST NOT expand `apply_expression_template` nodes except as rule 3 requires
clauses.note: After load, every non-eager (non-target-bearing) template reference survives unexpanded.

clauses.quote: downstream code MAY recognise them (that is the point), but MUST give them the semantics of rule 2
clauses.note: Any consumer's result on the reference-preserving tree equals its result on Expand(tree).

clauses.quote: pair MUST produce structurally identical ASTs with bit-equal constants; caching MUST NOT be observable
clauses.note: Expand is a pure function of (template, bindings): repeated expansions are structurally equal with bit-equal constants.

clauses.quote: All observable behavior MUST be as if evaluated on `Expand(tree)`; numeric results MUST be bit-identical to it
clauses.note: Evaluating a reference-preserving tree gives bit-identical results to evaluating Expand(tree).

clauses.quote: or whose own `bindings` carry such an op or a nested eager reference, MUST be expanded innermost-first in a pre-pass before the §9.6.3 fixpoint
clauses.note: Target-bearing references (and those whose bindings carry rewrite-target ops or eager references) are expanded innermost-first before the fixpoint, so no rewrite-target op survives inside a reference.

clauses.quote: A consumer whose *decisions* depend on the shape of an expression MUST therefore reach those decisions on `Expand(tree)`, not on the reference-preserving tree, or its behavior becomes a function of the author's factoring — which rule 2 forbids ("all observable behavior MUST be as if evaluated on `Expand(tree)`"). The projection-pushdown desugar (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.5.7) is the worked example: **whether the pushdown fires MUST NOT depend on whether the author factored the binning body through a template.**
clauses.note: Shape-dependent transforms (e.g. projection pushdown) make the same decision on a document and on its template-refactored equivalent.

clauses.quote: then materialized entries in lexicographic (UTF-8 byte) name order; all five bindings MUST emit this exact order
clauses.note: An emitted component expression_templates block lists authored entries in authored order, then materialized entries sorted by UTF-8 bytes of their names.

clauses.quote: a binding MUST treat a missing argument, a null argument, and an empty map identically
clauses.note: Load mode is generic iff the root is a template-library file and the loader binding set is empty; absent, null and empty select the same mode.

clauses.quote: `emit(load(f))` MUST parse deep-equal to `f`
clauses.note: On a generic load, an import-free template-library file round-trips to a document deep-equal to itself (no folding, nothing dropped or added).

clauses.quote: The modes MUST NOT be mixed.
clauses.note: Generic-load emit leaves every metaparameter site symbolic; instantiating-load emit folds every one; no emit is partially folded.

clauses.quote: **Load preservation.** `emit(load(f))` MUST reproduce `f`. Preservation is **full value equality**, not mere key presence: every member `f` authors — every object key, at every depth — MUST be present in the emitted document *with an equal value*
clauses.note: emit(load(f)) equals f modulo canonical serialization, omission of default/empty fields, and the enumerated required load-time rewrites.
clauses.concern: The 'only differences this rule admits' list omits differences the spec itself requires elsewhere: consumption of component expression_template_imports (§9.7.6), materialized registry entries added by rule 5, the esm version bump of rule 8, lowering of rewrite-target ops by the §9.6.3 fixpoint, and consumption of composition-form injections (§9.7.10); read literally, every conforming emit of a document with imports or match rules violates it.

clauses.quote: a binding applying one MUST still preserve every field outside the construct it rewrote
clauses.note: A permitted (optional) emit rewrite such as the §6.7.4 y-shorthand desugar changes only the construct it rewrites; all other fields are preserved with equal values.

clauses.quote: a conformance harness MUST assert the round-trip against the **original document**
clauses.note: Requirement on the conformance harness's comparison target, not on format semantics.

clauses.quote: Both modes MUST be idempotent. `emit ∘ load` MUST be a byte-wise fixed point within a mode
clauses.note: emit(load(emit(load(f)))) is byte-identical to emit(load(f)) when both loads use the same mode.

clauses.quote: bindings MUST discharge this via registration-time, call-site, and memoized per-instantiation checks (§9.6.9), not by materializing the full expansion
clauses.note: Implementation strategy (no full materialization) is a performance requirement; the semantic content, validity iff Expand(document) is valid, is not itself a MUST.

clauses.quote: `apply_expression_template` call site or any **materialized** registry entry MUST declare `esm: 0.9.0` or later
clauses.note: An emitted document containing a surviving call site or a materialized registry entry declares esm >= 0.9.0; otherwise it keeps the source version.

clauses.quote: Files declaring `esm: 0.3.x` or earlier MUST be rejected by all five bindings if they carry either construct, with diagnostic `apply_expression_template_version_too_old`.
clauses.note: A document declaring esm < 0.4.0 that carries expression_templates or apply_expression_template is rejected with apply_expression_template_version_too_old.

clauses.quote: Files declaring an earlier version MUST be rejected by all five bindings if they carry any of these constructs, with diagnostic `template_import_version_too_old`.
clauses.note: A document declaring esm < 0.8.0 that carries imports, top-level expression_templates or metaparameters is rejected with template_import_version_too_old.

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST emit the following stable diagnostic codes
clauses.note: Each condition in the §9.6.6 table is reported with exactly its listed code.

clauses.quote: The evaluator MUST NOT contract the range as empty
clauses.note: A range over a derived index set whose producer was not materialized yields derived_index_set_unmaterialized at build, never the semiring's additive identity.

clauses.quote: The check MUST precede evaluation
clauses.note: An expression containing an op the evaluator cannot evaluate is refused with unevaluable_operator before any part is evaluated, including ops in untaken ifelse branches.

clauses.quote: The diagnostic MUST name the offending op, and the evaluator MUST NOT evaluate the op to a sentinel value
clauses.note: unevaluable_operator names the op and evaluation never returns a number (NaN, zero, etc.) for it.

clauses.quote: Fires at BUILD, before evaluation, and MUST name the construct and the evaluator.
clauses.note: An evaluator that cannot run events, implicit equations or Wiener noise refuses at build with unsupported_construct naming both, rather than running without them.

clauses.quote: A parameter the caller pins with `p` IS bound, MUST build, and the pin MUST reach the right-hand side.
clauses.note: A data-fed parameter given a caller value builds, and the right-hand side reads that value.
clauses.concern: The data_source_unbound row says the code fires only 'in a case none of the following rules answers', but the rules that follow (default builds, no default is E_TREEWALK_MISSING_DATA, unresolved key is data_source_undefined, pinned builds) appear to cover every case, so the condition under which data_source_unbound is raised is undefined.

clauses.quote: Fires at construction, before anything is built, and MUST name the offending value.
clauses.note: Concerns the esm_problem compiler option of API_SPEC, not format semantics.

clauses.quote: The message MUST name what would have to be loaded or built. A binding MUST NOT answer by selecting a different compiler
clauses.note: Binding build/packaging capability and compiler selection API behaviour.

clauses.quote: Fires at BUILD, and MUST name the compiler, the **rule**
clauses.note: Compiler-specific refusal reporting; depends on which compiler a binding offers, not on document semantics.

clauses.quote: Fires at the call, before any integration, and MUST name the removed constructs' classes.
clauses.note: Host-API refusal on solve/init of a stripped Problem (API_SPEC §5.8); it governs a binding's call surface, not document semantics.

clauses.quote: Fires at `compile_kernels`, and MUST name the kernel and the output.
clauses.note: Validation of a compile_kernels spec (API_SPEC §5.8); the kernel spec is a host-API argument, not part of the document.

clauses.quote: Fires at `compile_kernels`, and MUST name the event and the variable.
clauses.note: Refusal raised only when an affect is compiled as a standalone kernel (API_SPEC §5.8); event semantics themselves are covered by the event clauses.

clauses.quote: Fires when the tile is built, and MUST name the rule, the variable, the axis and the missing cells.
clauses.note: Tile restriction is an API_SPEC §5.8 execution feature (range-restricted right-hand sides), not part of the format.

clauses.quote: loading MUST fail rather than leave the templates silently inert. The message MUST name the offending keys.
clauses.note: A document with top-level expression_templates beside models/reaction_systems/data_sources/coupling/domain is rejected with template_library_illegal_payload naming those keys.

clauses.quote: The message MUST name both contributors, both definitions, and the `index_set_rename` remedy.
clauses.note: The subsystem_index_set_conflict diagnostic carries both contributors and both definitions.

clauses.quote: MUST name the edge or construct. Refusing is REQUIRED
clauses.note: A declared element_type that a mount edge or evaluator construct cannot carry is refused with element_type_uncarried naming it, never evaluated in another precision.

clauses.quote: an unchecked `fn` is discarded silently rather than failing. Loading MUST fail.
clauses.note: A broadcast node with absent or non-scalar-operator fn, or an argument count outside that operator's arity, is rejected at load with invalid_broadcast_fn.

clauses.quote: All five bindings (Julia, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go) MUST produce a structurally-equal `reactions` array
clauses.note: Assertion about one fixed fixture; a test the model participates in, not a property (covered by the §9.6.4 rule-2 clauses).

clauses.quote: All five bindings MUST produce structurally-equal post-substitution nodes
clauses.note: Fixed-fixture assertion; the general property is spec.9.6.1.param-shadows-literal-substitute.

clauses.quote: All five bindings MUST produce structurally-equal expanded `ranges` tuples
clauses.note: Fixed-fixture assertion; the general property is spec.9.6.1.ranges-binding-admissible together with spec.9.6.1.param-shadows-literal-substitute.

clauses.quote: a compound `match` pattern whose shape only assembles across a surviving-reference boundary: MUST NOT fire
clauses.note: Fixed-fixture assertion of rule-4 opacity; the property belongs to the §9.6.4 rule-4 behaviour.

clauses.quote: MUST be lowered to a `faq` + `makearray` stencil by a `match` rewrite rule (§9.6) before evaluation
clauses.note: No spatial D reaches evaluation: after the fixpoint any remaining spatial D is rejected by the unlowered_operator gate.
clauses.concern: The clause prescribes the output form (faq + makearray stencil), but nothing checks the body a rule produces; a rule lowering D to any evaluable-core expression passes the gate, and §9.6.8's own grad_is_Dx example shows rules whose bodies are not stencils, so only 'eliminated before evaluation' is enforceable.

clauses.quote: Two bindings expanding the same file MUST produce byte-identical post-lowering ASTs
clauses.note: Discretization lowering is a deterministic function of the document (same as the §9.6.3 fixpoint determinism, including identical rejections).

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST discharge this **without materializing the full expansion**
clauses.note: Performance/implementation requirement; the semantic half is that validity equals validity of Expand(document).

clauses.quote: so dotted names validate — binding resolvers MUST accept them
clauses.note: Template registry keys and apply_expression_template names may be dotted identifiers and resolve like any other name.

clauses.quote: or one whose index sets would put one name on two axes. Each MUST be rejected with `array_shape_mismatch`
clauses.note: An elementwise template application whose array arguments read in value positions have incomparable index sets, name an index set outside the target's declared shape, or would put one index set on two axes is rejected with array_shape_mismatch.

clauses.quote: `array_shape_mismatch` for an elementwise application MUST be decided at build
clauses.note: The elementwise shape checks run on the flattened system, after coupling: an explicit exception to the §4.3.4 validation-time rule, so validate() of a component alone does not decide them.

clauses.quote: An argument read in a value position MUST be a scalar or an array over declared index sets
clauses.note: Every array an application reads in a value position of its expansion is a variable over declared, inferred or coupled index sets, or an elementwise expression of such variables.

clauses.quote: every evaluating binding MUST reject it at build with `array_shape_mismatch`
clauses.note: A const array literal or a reshape result read in a value position of a template application's expansion is rejected at build with array_shape_mismatch.

clauses.quote: Every binding's flatten MUST therefore write the lift above into the flattened equations themselves
clauses.note: Flatten writes each elementwise template application, in an equation or a field initial condition, as the per-cell faq the build would lift it to, so the flattened system written out and read back denotes the same system. A variable declared shape [] is never lifted; when the lift refuses any right-hand side, nothing is lifted.

clauses.quote: It MUST NOT declare `models`, `reaction_systems`, `data_sources`, `coupling`, or `domain`
clauses.note: A document with top-level expression_templates and any of models/reaction_systems/data_sources/coupling/domain is rejected with template_library_illegal_payload.

clauses.quote: a binding without remote support MUST reject them with `template_import_unresolved`
clauses.note: Remote fetch is a binding I/O capability, not format semantics.

clauses.quote: A reference in a body denotes its expansion exactly as at any other site (§9.6.4 rule 2). `match` patterns MUST NOT contain `apply_expression_template` nodes.
clauses.note: Restates spec.9.6.3.match-no-apply-node: a match pattern containing an apply node is rejected at registration.

clauses.quote: `type` is required and MUST be `"integer"` (the only kind).
clauses.note: A metaparameter declaration whose type is missing or not "integer" is rejected.

clauses.quote: A metaparameter name MUST NOT collide with any variable, parameter, species, or index-set name visible in the document, nor with any **loop symbol** in it
clauses.note: A metaparameter whose name equals a visible variable/parameter/species/index-set name or any loop symbol (ranges key or output_idx entry, including in own and imported templates, checked in the library's own scope) is rejected with metaparameter_name_conflict.

clauses.quote: `/` MUST divide exactly, and overflow is an error (`metaparameter_type_error`)
clauses.note: Folding a metaparameter expression uses exact 64-bit integer arithmetic; an inexact division or an overflow is rejected with metaparameter_type_error.
clauses.concern: 'exact 64-bit integer arithmetic' does not say signed or unsigned, which fixes where overflow occurs; unary minus suggests signed int64 but it is not stated.

clauses.quote: a structural string field of an Expression node holds a *name*, not a reference to a value, and MUST be copied verbatim even when a bound metaparameter spells it exactly
clauses.note: Metaparameter substitution rewrites only expression positions; a structural string field equal to a bound metaparameter name is unchanged.

clauses.quote: the node `{"op": "grad", "args": ["x"], "dim": "x"}` MUST become `{"op": "grad", "args": [3], "dim": "x"}`
clauses.note: wrt, dim and integral's var are never substituted, while operand occurrences of the same name are.

clauses.quote: the node `{"op": "max", "args": ["k", "max"]}` MUST become `{"op": "max", "args": ["k", 3]}`
clauses.note: op, id and expect_cadence are never substituted.

clauses.quote: MUST keep `"reduce": "max"` while any `"max"` in its `expr` folds to 3
clauses.note: reduce, semiring, manifold, fn, table, side, attrs, members, from_faq and where are never substituted.

clauses.quote: the join clause `{"on": [["row_id", "row_id"]], "syms": ["i", "j"]}` MUST stay as written
clauses.note: Loop-symbol, reference, enum, unit and free-text fields are never substituted.

clauses.quote: so the set it holds MUST equal `skip_keys` in `tests/metaparameter_substitution/field_classification.json`
clauses.note: Metaparameter substitution skips exactly the object keys in skip_keys (map keys in name_keyed_map_keys are never tested against it).
clauses.concern: The normative structural key set is delegated to a test-data file outside the spec, so the spec text alone does not determine substitution; nothing states which wins if that file disagrees with the four families enumerated in the preceding paragraph.

clauses.quote: Consequently a subsystem-edge binding value's free names MUST already be closed in the mounting scope.
clauses.note: A subsystem-edge binding value folds immediately against the mounting document's closed metaparameters; a free name absent from that scope is template_import_unknown_name.
clauses.concern: Defaults apply only at the root's close (site 5) and a non-root document may leave metaparameters open for its importer (site 2), so a non-root mounting document's names need not be closed when its refs resolve; the clause does not say what happens then or which diagnostic applies to a declared-but-still-open name.

clauses.quote: A `rename` key MUST name a member of that set
clauses.note: A rename key outside the edge's surviving export set (templates after only, index sets, metaparameters left open by bindings) is rejected with template_import_rename_unknown_name.

clauses.quote: Targets (and `prefix`) MUST be dotted identifiers
clauses.note: A prefix or rename target not matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)* is rejected with template_import_rename_invalid.

clauses.quote: Within each namespace (templates, index sets, metaparameters) the post-rename names MUST be distinct
clauses.note: Edge renaming is injective within each namespace, else template_import_rename_collision.

clauses.quote: but bindings that compose lazily MUST rewrite them
clauses.note: Renaming a template rewrites every apply_expression_template.name reference to it in the surviving imported declarations.
clauses.concern: The parenthetical says references are 'in practice already inlined by the target's own §9.7.3 composition', but §9.7.3 says bodies are not inlined from esm 0.9.0; under the current model every binding must rewrite these references, not only those that 'compose lazily'.

clauses.quote: A `rebind` key MUST occur free in the surviving declarations
clauses.note: A rebind key that does not occur free, or names a declared name, is template_import_rebind_unknown_name; one naming a bound index symbol is template_import_rename_invalid.

clauses.quote: Targets MUST be fresh — colliding with a remaining free name
clauses.note: A rebind target equal to a remaining free name, bound index symbol, template param or another target is rejected with template_import_rename_collision.

clauses.quote: the injected `ref` MUST resolve to a template-library file (§9.7.1)
clauses.note: An injected import whose ref is not a template-library file is rejected with template_import_not_library.

clauses.quote: A test's injection MUST NOT run at component load
clauses.note: Loading a document never applies Test/Analysis injections: the component's rewrite-targets and the emitted document are unchanged by them.

clauses.quote: For an array `xs` of `n` entries, `n` below 2^53, `searchsorted(x, xs, n)` MUST evaluate to 1 plus the number of `k` in `[1, n]` for which `xs[k] >= x` is false.
clauses.note: searchsorted(x, xs, n) = 1 + #{k : not(xs[k] >= x)}; on non-decreasing xs the least index with xs[i] >= x, n+1 if none (NaN x included), 1 for n = 0.

clauses.quote: For `table` and `axis` of `n >= 2` entries each, `axis` strictly increasing, `linear(table, axis, x, n)` MUST evaluate to `table[1]` when `x <= axis[1]`, to `table[n]` when `x >= axis[n]`, and otherwise to `table[i] + ((x - axis[i]) / (axis[i+1] - axis[i])) * (table[i+1] - table[i])`, each operation rounded once in that order, where `i` is the number of `k` in `[1, n]` with `axis[k] <= x`, held to `[1, n - 1]`.
clauses.note: linear: flat edge values outside the axis, else the pinned blend with the clamped count index; NaN x gives NaN.

clauses.quote: For a row-major `table` of `nx` rows of `ny` entries and strictly increasing axes `axis_x` (`nx >= 2`) and `axis_y` (`ny >= 2`), `bilinear(table, axis_x, axis_y, x, y, nx, ny)` MUST first clamp each query to its axis: `cx` is `axis_x[1]` when `x <= axis_x[1]`, `axis_x[nx]` when `x >= axis_x[nx]`, and `x` otherwise, and `cy` likewise from `y`.
clauses.note: bilinear: queries clamped to the axes, clamped count indices, two x-blends then the y-blend in the pinned order; NaN in either query gives NaN.

clauses.quote: Each public template of `lib/calendar.esm` (`year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `day_of_year`, `julian_day`, `is_leap_year`, `seconds_since_midnight`) MUST evaluate to NaN for a NaN or infinite `t` and for a finite `t` with `|t| >= 2^52` s.
clauses.note: Every public calendar template is NaN for NaN, infinite or |t| >= 2^52 s.

clauses.quote: For finite `t` with `|t| < 2^52` s, the integer templates MUST evaluate exactly, in binary64, to the field of the UTC instant `t`: `year` the proleptic-Gregorian year in astronomical numbering (0 is 1 BC); `month` in 1..12 (1 is January); `day` the day of the month in 1..31; `hour` in 0..23; `minute` in 0..59; `second` in 0..59 (no leap-second slot); `day_of_year` in 1..366 (1 is January 1); `is_leap_year` 1 when the year is divisible by 4 and not by 100 unless by 400, else 0; and `seconds_since_midnight` the whole second of the day `s`, in 0..86399, in seconds.
clauses.note: On |t| < 2^52 s the integer calendar templates are the exact proleptic-Gregorian fields of t (ranges stated), in binary64.

clauses.quote: For finite `t` with `|t| < 2^52` s, `julian_day(t)` MUST evaluate to `(d + 2440588) + ((s - 43200) + (t - floor(t))) / 86400`, each operation rounded once in that order: the Julian Date of `t`, including the fraction of the day.
clauses.note: julian_day is the pinned binary64 formula on the exact split, each operation rounded once in order.

clauses.quote: For `n >= 1`, `argmin(f, n)` MUST evaluate to the index of the first NaN candidate when some `v_k` is NaN, and otherwise to the least `k` at which `v_k` equals the minimum of the candidates. `argmax(f, n)` MUST evaluate the same way with the maximum.
clauses.note: argmin/argmax for n >= 1: first NaN candidate if any, else least index of the extremum; n = 0 gives +Inf.

clauses.quote: `argmin_where(f, p, n)` MUST evaluate to `n + 1` when no `k` in `[1, n]` satisfies the predicate `p` (so `n = 0` gives 1), and otherwise to `argmin` over the candidates that do: the first such `k` whose `v_k` is NaN when one is NaN, else the least such `k` at which `v_k` equals their minimum. `argmax_where(f, p, n)` MUST evaluate the same way with the maximum.
clauses.note: argmin_where/argmax_where: n + 1 when no candidate passes p; else the argmin/argmax rule over the passing candidates.

clauses.quote: `pair_key(a, b, lo_a, lo_b, n_a, n_b)` MUST evaluate to `(a - lo_a) * n_b + (b - lo_b)` when `a` and `b` are integers with `lo_a <= a < lo_a + n_a` and `lo_b <= b < lo_b + n_b`, and to NaN (`0 / 0`) otherwise, including when either is NaN.
clauses.note: pair_key is (a - lo_a) n_b + (b - lo_b) for in-range integers, NaN otherwise; exact for magnitudes <= 2^25; lexicographic order.

clauses.quote: `edge_key(u, v, lo, n)` MUST evaluate to `pair_key(min(u, v), max(u, v), lo, lo, n, n)`, so it gives the same value with `u` and `v` swapped, NaN included.
clauses.note: edge_key is pair_key of (min, max); symmetric in u, v including NaN.

clauses.quote: `rank_of(x, members, n)` MUST evaluate to 1 plus the number of `k` in `[1, n]` for which `members[k] >= x` is false, and `rank_of_set(x, members, S)` to the same count over the positions of the index set `S` in place of `[1, n]`.
clauses.note: rank_of / rank_of_set = 1 + #{k : not(members[k] >= x)}; on ascending members equal to searchsorted.

clauses.quote: The overlap templates MUST be applied to convex polygons, and on the sphere to polygons that each lie within a hemisphere.
clauses.note: The overlap templates' contract covers convex polygons (each within a hemisphere on the sphere) only; no check, no claim otherwise.

clauses.quote: `overlap_area_planar` MUST evaluate to 0 when the orientation fan sum of either ring is exactly 0, and otherwise to the sum, over every edge `p -> q` of each polygon, of `s · max(0, t1 - t0) · ((p - o) × (q - o)) / 2`, where `o` is the first vertex of A, `s` is the sign of the edge's polygon's fan sum (+1 when it is `>= 0`), `(u × w)` is `u_x w_y - u_y w_x`, and `[t0, t1]` is the part of the edge inside the other polygon: `t0` the `max` and `t1` the `min`, over that polygon's edges, of the bounds each one's closed half-plane imposes on the chord parameter. For two convex polygons this is the area of their intersection, in squared coordinate units.
clauses.note: overlap_area_planar: 0 on a zero fan sum, else the edge-clipping Green's-theorem sum about the first vertex of A.

clauses.quote: In the planar template a vertex `p` MUST count as on the line of edge `a -> b` when `|(b - a) × (p - a)|` is at most `1e-12 · L1(b - a) · (L1(p) + L1(q) + L1(a))`, with `p -> q` the edge being clipped and `L1` the sum of absolute coordinates.
clauses.note: Planar on-the-line test: |cross| <= 1e-12 L1(b - a)(L1(p) + L1(q) + L1(a)); collinear edges count once same way, not at all opposite.

clauses.quote: `overlap_area_spherical` MUST evaluate the same construction on the unit sphere, with great-circle edges: 0 when either fan sum is exactly 0; the side of a point `p` against edge `a -> b` is `(a × b) · p`, on the great circle when its magnitude is at most `1e-14`; and an edge `a -> q` clipped to `[t0, t1]` contributes `s · (F(t1) - F(t0))` when `t1 > t0` and nothing otherwise, where `F(t)` is the signed solid angle, `2 · atan2(...)` in the Van Oosterom-Strackee form, of the spherical triangle with corners `o`, `a` and the chord point `a + t (q - a)`.
clauses.note: overlap_area_spherical: the same construction on the unit sphere with side (a x b).p, tolerance 1e-14, Van Oosterom-Strackee contributions.

clauses.quote: A vertex repeated exactly (an explicit closing duplicate, or the rectangular-storage padding of a cell with fewer vertices than its stack has slots) makes a zero-length edge, which contributes exactly zero and bounds nothing. For finite coordinates `overlap_area_planar` MUST therefore give the same binary64 value on a padded ring as on the unpadded one.
clauses.note: Exactly repeated vertices (padding) leave overlap_area_planar's binary64 value unchanged.

clauses.quote: `lonlat_to_unit(ring, cell, vert, comp)` MUST evaluate, with `lon = ring[cell, vert, 1]` and `lat = ring[cell, vert, 2]` in degrees and `c` the binary64 constant `0.017453292519943295` (π/180), to `cos(lat · c) · cos(lon · c)` for `comp = 1`, `cos(lat · c) · sin(lon · c)` for `comp = 2`, and `sin(lat · c)` for any other `comp`.
clauses.note: lonlat_to_unit component formulas with the binary64 pi/180 constant; comp other than 1, 2 gives sin(lat).

clauses.quote: Writing it MUST produce the same flattened system as omitting it
clauses.note: A translate value of "B._var" yields the same flattened system as omitting the entry.

clauses.quote: so the two spellings denote the same variable and MUST produce the same flattened system
clauses.note: A bare translate endpoint resolved against its side's system flattens identically to its fully scoped spelling.

clauses.quote: `to` MUST already have one — see below
clauses.note: Table form of spec.10.3.multiplicative-no-tendency: a multiplicative connector target must have a D(to) equation.

clauses.quote: a library MUST raise `couple_multiplicative_no_tendency` rather than silently dropping the connector equation
clauses.note: A multiplicative connector equation whose target has no D(to) equation in the flattened system is rejected with couple_multiplicative_no_tendency.

clauses.quote: every variable reference MUST be a fully-scoped reference (`System.var`) resolvable in the flattened coupled system
clauses.note: Every free variable reference in an Expression transform is System.var and resolves in the flattened system.
clauses.concern: A regridding transform is a faq whose bound index symbols (and possibly t or metaparameter names) appear as bare strings in variable-reference positions; the clause does not exempt them, and no diagnostic is named for a violation.

clauses.quote: The expression MUST reference the entry's `from` variable
clauses.note: An Expression transform contains at least one reference to the entry's from variable.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is named, and it is unclear whether a reference reaching `from` only through an apply_expression_template binding (as in the §10.5 example) counts, i.e. whether the check runs on the reference-preserving tree or on Expand(tree).

clauses.quote: a library edge's transform MUST expand to an already-lowered form
clauses.note: A coupling-library edge transform whose templates would introduce grad/div/spatial D is rejected with coupling_library_illegal_payload.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST therefore apply the scoping in the same pass that namespaces the component's equations
clauses.note: The flattened template registry equals merge(scope(each component's carried registry)), with dedup on post-scoping bodies and DAG-propagated owner-path renames.

clauses.quote: A caller that goes on to namespace MUST compose it with the scoping
clauses.note: Obligation on callers of a binding's flatten_template_registries API surface, not on format semantics.

clauses.quote: Each map key MUST name a system **referenced by that entry**
clauses.note: A coupling-entry expression_template_imports key that names no system the entry references is rejected with template_inject_target_unknown.

clauses.quote: A coupling-library file **MUST NOT** declare `models`, `reaction_systems`, `data_sources`,
clauses.note: A document with coupling_roles and any of models/reaction_systems/data_sources/domain/index_sets/metaparameters/expression_templates is rejected with coupling_library_illegal_payload.

clauses.quote: It MUST NOT contain a `callback` entry
clauses.note: A coupling library containing a callback entry or an edge with expression_template_imports is rejected with coupling_library_illegal_payload.

clauses.quote: A coupling-library file **MUST NOT** itself contain a `coupling_import` entry
clauses.note: A coupling library containing a coupling_import entry is rejected with coupling_library_nested_import.

clauses.quote: a library transform MUST expand to an already-lowered form
clauses.note: Same as spec.10.4.library-transform-lowered: a library edge transform template introducing a rewrite-target op is coupling_library_illegal_payload.

clauses.quote: **Every role MUST have a `bind` entry.**
clauses.note: A declared role absent from bind is rejected with coupling_import_role_unbound.

clauses.quote: **Every `bind` key MUST name a declared role.**
clauses.note: A bind key that is not a declared role is rejected with coupling_import_unknown_role.

clauses.quote: **Every `bind` value MUST resolve to a component.**
clauses.note: A bind value not resolving to a top-level or nested model/reaction system is rejected with coupling_import_bind_not_a_component.

clauses.quote: `s₁` MUST name a top-level `models` / `reaction_systems` key, and each subsequent `sᵢ` MUST name a key in the preceding system's `subsystems` map. The whole path MUST terminate on a system node
clauses.note: A bind value resolves iff its first segment is a top-level model/reaction system and each later segment is a subsystems key of the previous one; data_sources entries never resolve.

clauses.quote: a library MUST NOT hide a component reference there
clauses.note: Authoring policy on library files: config is opaque and copied verbatim, so no check can observe a violation.

clauses.quote: MUST apply the coupled-system reference validation to the **expanded** coupling
clauses.note: After coupling_import expansion, a bound component lacking a referenced variable fails with unresolved_scoped_ref naming Component.var.

clauses.quote: MUST report it at the pointer of the `coupling_import` entry (`/coupling/<i>`)
clauses.note: A mis-bind reported by validate on the source document carries the pointer /coupling/<i> of the import entry.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT substitute `0.0` (or any other value it chose) for the missing one, and MUST NOT defer the failure to the solve.
clauses.note: Problem construction with a parameter that has no default and no supplied value fails with E_TREEWALK_MISSING_DATA naming it, before any solve.

clauses.quote: A runtime that cannot honour the declaration for some construct MUST **error naming that construct**
clauses.note: Evaluation under a declared element_type either rounds per that precision at every operation or errors naming the construct; it never silently uses another precision.

clauses.quote: MUST be an error naming both variables (`mixed_element_type`)
clauses.note: Static precision propagation: an operator with operands of different declared element types, or an equation whose RHS precision differs from its LHS, is rejected with mixed_element_type.
clauses.concern: Operands are arbitrary sub-expressions whose precision is inferred from leaves, not necessarily variables, so 'naming both variables' is undefined when an operand is compound or when several variables of each precision feed it.

clauses.quote: Exempting a variable only where its data ENTERS is not sufficient and MUST NOT be offered as an implementation of this field
clauses.note: A variable's element_type governs the precision of every operation over it, not only the rounding where its data enters.

clauses.quote: Those symbols are implicitly declared and MUST NOT be reported as `undefined_variable` (§4.9.1).
clauses.note: Spatial coordinate names in an ic RHS are not undefined_variable.
clauses.concern: The set of 'spatial coordinate names' is given only by example (x, y, z, lon, lat, lev, 'not necessarily the index-set key'), so which bare names an ic RHS may use without being undefined_variable is not defined.

clauses.quote: a binding MUST NOT start such an unknown at `0.0` (or any other value it chose), and MUST NOT defer the failure to the solve
clauses.note: Problem construction with an ODE state or algebraic unknown that gets no starting value from any source fails with E_TREEWALK_MISSING_INITIAL_VALUE naming it, before any solve.

clauses.quote: An `ic` equation MUST NOT be placed inside a reaction system's `constraint_equations`
clauses.note: An ic equation anywhere other than a model's equations is rejected with ic_in_reaction_system.

clauses.quote: A build MUST refuse it at construction with the diagnostic code **`ic_reads_state`**
clauses.note: An ic right-hand side that reads an ODE state or algebraic unknown, directly or through a chain of observeds, is refused at construction with ic_reads_state naming the target, the state and the chain.

clauses.quote: A build MUST NOT evaluate such a right-hand side with the state at a placeholder value
clauses.note: Such an ic is never evaluated with the state at 0, its default or any other stand-in value.

clauses.quote: an inline-test `reference` still MUST NOT mention `t` free
clauses.note: Restates spec.6.6.5.reference-free-t: the start-of-run additions do not extend to an inline-test reference.
